Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 114, verses 1–6:

On the interpretation of His words, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind (1), the King of mankind (2), the God of mankind (3), from the evil of the sneaking whisperer (4) who whispers in the breasts of mankind (5), of the jinn and of mankind (6).﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, "I seek protection" ﴿in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind﴾, and He is the King of all creation, both humans and jinn and other than them. This is to inform those who used to glorify people with the glorification of believers toward their Lord that He is the King of whoever they glorify, that this is within His dominion and authority, over which His power operates, and that He is more deserving of glorification and more worthy of worship than whoever among other people is glorified and worshipped.

* *

As for His words: ﴿the God of mankind﴾

He says: the one worshipped by mankind, to whom worship is due instead of anything else besides Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿from the evil of the whisperer﴾

It means: from the evil of the devil ﴿the sneaking one﴾ who withdraws once and whispers another time, and he withdraws, as has been mentioned, when the servant remembers his Lord.

Mention of those who said this:

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Every child is born with the whisperer upon his heart. When he understands and remembers God, he withdraws; and when he is heedless, he whispers. He said: That is His saying: ﴿the whisperer, the sneaking one﴾.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the whisperer, the sneaking one﴾, he said: The devil squats upon the heart of the son of Adam; when he forgets and is heedless, he whispers, and when he remembers God, he withdraws.

• He said: Mahran narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the whisperer, the sneaking one﴾, he said: He spreads out, and when he remembers God he withdraws and contracts; when he is heedless, he spreads out again.

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the whisperer, the sneaking one﴾, he said: The devil is upon the heart of the human being; when he remembers God, he withdraws.

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿the whisperer﴾, he said: It is the devil, and he is also the sneaking one; when the servant remembers his Lord he withdraws, and he whispers and withdraws.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿from the evil of the whisperer, the sneaking one﴾, meaning: the devil, who whispers in the breast of the son of Adam and withdraws when God is mentioned.

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from his father, who said: It has been related to me that the devil, or he said the whisperer, breathes into the heart of the human being at times of sorrow and at times of joy, and when God is mentioned he withdraws.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿the sneaking one﴾: The sneaking one is the one who whispers once and withdraws once, from among the jinn and mankind. It was said: the devil of mankind is more severe upon people than the devil of the jinn; the devil of the jinn whispers and you do not see him, but this one confronts you face to face.

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to say about it: ﴿from the evil of the whisperer﴾ who whispers, by calling to obedience to him, into the breasts of people, until he is answered in what he calls to of his obedience; and when he is answered in that, he withdraws.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the whisperer﴾, he said: It is the devil who commands him; when he is obeyed, he withdraws.

The correct statement on this matter, in my view, is to say: Allah commanded His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to seek refuge in Him from the evil of a devil who whispers once and withdraws another time. He did not restrict his whispering to one type of it, nor his withdrawing to one manner rather than another. He may whisper by calling to disobedience to Allah, and when he is obeyed in it, he withdraws; and he may whisper by forbidding obedience to Allah, and when the servant remembers his Lord's command and obeys Him in it, and disobeys the devil, he withdraws. So he is, in both his states, a whisperer who withdraws, and this is his description.

* *

As for His words: ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾

It means by this: the devil, the whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, both jinn and humans.

If someone says: the jinn are men, so how is it said "who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind"? It is answered: Allah has named them "mankind" in this place, just as He named them "men" in another place, when He said: ﴿And there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾. So He made the jinn men, and likewise He made some of them "mankind," and so it is with what occurs in the revelation of this kind.

It has been mentioned that some of the Arabs said, while narrating, that a group of jinn came and stopped, and it was asked: Who are you? They said: "Mankind from the jinn." So He made some of them "mankind," and so it is with what occurs in the revelation of this kind.

End of the book of tafsir, and praise be to Allah, the Most High, the Great.

It was said: the devil of mankind is more severe upon people than the devil of the jinn; the devil of the jinn whispers and you do not see him, but this one confronts you face to face.

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to say about it: ﴿from the evil of the whisperer﴾ who whispers, by calling to obedience to him, into the breasts of people, until he is answered in what he calls to of his obedience; and when he is answered in that, he withdraws.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the whisperer﴾, he said: It is the devil who commands him; when he is obeyed, he withdraws.

The correct statement on this matter, in my view, is to say: Allah commanded His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to seek refuge in Him from the evil of a devil who whispers once and withdraws another time. He did not restrict his whispering to one type of it, nor his withdrawing to one manner rather than another. He may whisper by calling to disobedience to Allah, and when he is obeyed in it, he withdraws; and he may whisper by forbidding obedience to Allah, and when the servant remembers his Lord's command and obeys Him in it, and disobeys the devil, he withdraws. So he is, in both his states, a whisperer who withdraws, and this is his description.

* *

As for His words: ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾

It means by this: the devil, the whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, both jinn and humans.

If someone says: the jinn are men, so how is it said "who whispers in the breasts of mankind, of the jinn and of mankind"? It is answered: Allah has named them "mankind" in this place, just as He named them "men" in another place, when He said: ﴿And there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾. So He made the jinn men, and likewise He made some of them "mankind," and so it is with what occurs in the revelation of this kind.

It has been mentioned that some of the Arabs said, while narrating, that a group of jinn came and stopped, and it was asked: Who are you? They said: "Mankind from the jinn." So He made some of them "mankind," and so it is with what occurs in the revelation of this kind.

End of the book of tafsir, and praise be to Allah, the Most High, the Great.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 114, verses 1–6:

On the interpretation of His words, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind (1), the King of mankind (2), the God of mankind (3), from the evil of the sneaking whisperer (4) who whispers in the breasts of mankind (5), of the jinn and of mankind (6).﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, "I seek protection" ﴿in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind﴾, and He is the King of all creation, both humans and jinn and other than them. This is to inform those who used to glorify people with the glorification of believers toward their Lord that He is the King of whoever they glorify, that this is within His dominion and authority, over which His power operates, and that He is more deserving of glorification and more worthy of worship than whoever among other people is glorified and worshipped.

* *

He says: the one worshipped by mankind, to whom worship is due instead of anything else besides Him.
